one_month_reasoning: I built this 1-month distribution myself rather than reusing round 1's. Window events: Q3 2026 earnings on Oct 28 before the open (guide $9.3-9.4B sales, $0.70-0.71 split-adjusted EPS) and the late-October hyperscaler Q3 capex prints. Model: about 20 non-earnings trading days at ~2.2%/day with fat tails (Student-t, 5 df; 10% monthly sd, which is below the 46%/3.5 = 13% headline because the 1-year figure includes the Jan-May swings; recent Aug-Sep daily moves run ~2%), plus a two-state earnings-day jump. In the beat state (72%) the jump is +4.5% ± 3%, matching the verified +3.6% (Oct-25), +3.2% (Apr-26) and +4.5% then +6.3% (Jul-26) reactions. In the sell-off state (28%) it is -8.5% ± 4%, matching the -12.2% on a beat in Jan-26. A small -0.3% drift offsets the +10% run from $77.55 on Sep 18 to $85.67 (short-term reversal risk). Result: median ~$86.6 (+1%), mean ~$86.8, and a left tail fatter than the right: P(>=77.10) = 0.83, while P(>=94.24) = 0.21.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: Oct-2027 NTM EPS $3.62 x 24x = $86.9 (includes a ~1% haircut for the risk that Foxconn Interconnect takes Kyber midplane share in 2028). 40% FCF yield: $3.40 / 3.75% = $90.7. Blend ~$88.6.

bear.story: AI capex digests in 2028 (Goldman +12%, UBS +6%), and the market starts pricing the loss of Kyber midplane content to Foxconn Interconnect (GF Securities) for the 2028 ramp. Book-to-bill drops below 1, IT datacom stalls, and the multiple falls to ~18x on ~$3.15 EPS. The verified 20% drawdown in three weeks after Q1 2026 shows how quickly that can happen.

base.story: 2027 roughly in line with consensus: revenue ~$42B, EPS ~$3.3, margins ~29%. Oberon/NVL72 copper demand is extended through 2027 by the Kyber delay, and CommScope optics adds to growth. The multiple compresses to ~24x NTM as growth slows to the teens.

bull.story: 2027 capex lands at or above $1.2-1.4T and 2028 keeps growing double digits. The extended Oberon life and power interconnect content beat plan, Kyber content risk proves smaller than GF suggests, NTM EPS reaches $4.2+, and the market holds ~28x.

thesis_break_reason: $59 is ~31% below spot and just under the $59.6 closing floor that held twice in 2026 (Mar 30, May 19, Twelve Data). That is ~18x 2027 consensus EPS. A break there would most likely mean estimate cuts: book-to-bill below 1 for two quarters, a hyperscaler capex cut, or confirmation of lost Nvidia rack content (Kyber midplane to Foxconn Interconnect) without an offset elsewhere. A rotation alone would not explain it.

reasoning: Round 2. Round-1 facts stand: 2:1 split on 2026-09-03; Q2-26 sales $8.8B (+30% organic), adj EPS $0.675, book-to-bill 1.23; Q3 guide $9.3-9.4B / $0.70-0.71; net debt $14.1B; ~2.58B diluted shares. The supervisor raised three points. (1) The GF Securities report that Nvidia may have replaced APH with Foxconn Interconnect as the major Kyber midplane connector supplier. I confirmed the headline (MSN/Intellectia) but not its date. I also found what it leaves out: on Jul 6 2026 SemiAnalysis reported Kyber slipped to 2028 over midplane PCB problems, and 2027 Rubin Ultra stays on Oberon/NVL72. TechFlow's winners/losers summary names Amphenol a relative beneficiary of the longer copper-cartridge life, and a Jefferies note quoted on X says the supply chain had seen this coming since May. Nvidia replied only that its 'roadmap remains intact'. So I agree the GF report is a real left-tail input, but I disagree that it is a 2027 issue. It mostly bites in 2028+, which the stock will start to price by Oct 2027, so I give it a ~1% NTM EPS haircut and a slightly heavier bear leg rather than a large shift. (2) Earnings-reaction asymmetry (+3.6/-12.2/+3.2/+4.5%) is verified, so I built it explicitly into a new, independent 1-month model. (3) Thin Polymarket markets (~$9k volume) now get zero weight. Their removal is offset by the GF and drawdown evidence, so the bear weight stays at 22%. 12-month distribution: 78% lognormal with median $92.5, sigma 0.35, plus 22% bear lognormal with median $63, sigma 0.38. That gives median ~$86, mean ~$91.6, and P(>=86) = 0.50. Fair value is $88.6 (from $88.8), roughly at spot: EPS growth is offset by multiple compression from 29x to ~24x. Limits: MSN, Intellectia and CNBC blocked fetching, so the Kyber delay comes from Tom's Hardware/DCD headlines, a KuCoin/TechFlow summary and Benzinga. X posts appear only as search snippets. Only 11 of 24 sources are in-lane (below the 60% target) because the supervisor's follow-ups pointed to press and sell-side items. No option data was used.
